content.title: About
content.content: Top sirloin is a post‑rib cut from the rear back portion of the cow. It is a lean, flavorful steak with a firm texture, commonly used for grilling, pan‑searing, or quick roasting.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Top sirloin is considered one of the most tender cuts after filet mignon.
It contains less fat than most other steak cuts, making it popular among calorie‑conscious eaters.
In the United States it is often called “New York strip” or “Kansas City strip.”
The meat holds its juices well when cooked properly.
Raw top sirloin can be used for steak tartare and carpaccio.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Top sirloin provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich source of iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin that support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals contribute to immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Top sirloin has virtually no carbs, fitting well into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella); proper cooking is required.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Although leaner than many cuts, it still contains saturated fat, which should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of red meat can be hard to digest for sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Top sirloin is most often cooked as a steak: sear on high heat for 2–3 minutes per side to the desired doneness. It can also be grilled, oven‑roasted, or quickly pan‑seared. Raw cut is suitable for steak tartare, carpaccio, or marinating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw top sirloin refrigerated at 0‑4 °C, wrapped in plastic film or an airtight container, and use within 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 6‑12 months. Thaw frozen steak in the refrigerator before cooking.
